source: Andries Brouwer's database of Go games, https://homepages.cwi.nl/~aeb/go/games

categories.title: Learn on 9×9
categories.blurb: Short games on the small board, played by professionals. They are the quickest way to see how a whole game fits together.

games.title: The 25-move game
games.note: Black wins by resignation after only 25 moves: a quick lesson in how sharply a 9×9 fight can end.

games.title: The 30-move game
games.note: White (Iyama Yuta) wins by resignation in 30 moves, the shortest of the four celebration games for his six titles.

games.title: Iyama Yuta wins in 36 moves
games.note: Iyama Yuta, who became one of Japan's strongest players, wins as White by resignation (2003).

games.title: A young Iyama Yuta plays Black
games.note: Iyama (Black) beats Mochizuki Kenichi by resignation after 53 moves (2003).

games.title: Iyama beats Murakawa Daisuke
games.note: White (Iyama Yuta) wins by resignation after 52 moves (2009).

games.title: A close game for a six-title celebration
games.note: Iyama Yuta, as White, wins by a point and a half (2013).

games.title: A half-point game
games.note: Black wins by half a point after 51 moves, the smallest margin there is (1989).

games.title: A 41-move win
games.note: Black wins by resignation after 41 moves (1989).

games.title: Half a point decides it
games.note: Black wins by half a point in 39 moves.

games.title: A big win on a small board
games.note: White wins by 7.5 points (2002).

games.title: A one-and-a-half point game
games.note: Black wins by 1.5 after 55 moves, in a women's 9×9 match (2008).

games.title: The longest 9×9 game here
games.note: 89 moves; Black wins by 1.5 (2008).

games.title: A celebration game
games.note: Played for the 50th anniversary of the Nihon Ki-in Central Branch (2005); White wins by resignation after 54 moves.
games.event: 50th Anniversary of Nihon Ki-in Central Branch

games.title: Eight players against Cho Chikun
games.note: A team of eight plays Cho Chikun at a celebration of the Kitani school's 500 dan (2000). Cho wins as White in 40 moves.
games.black: Kim Sujun & Kobayashi Izumi & Inori Yoko & Umezawa Yukari & Hosaka Mayu & Hans Pietsch & Takemiya Yoko & Kono Rin

games.title: Go Seigen on 9×9
games.note: The legendary Go Seigen (Black) beats Miyamoto Naoki by 4 in 53 moves (1968).

games.title: Miyamoto beats Go Seigen
games.note: Miyamoto Naoki, Black, beats Go Seigen by 4 in 80 moves (1968).

categories.title: Handicap and teaching games
categories.blurb: Handicap stones let a weaker player take Black with a head start. These games show how the stones are used, from two to nine.

games.title: Two stones
games.note: A professional handicap game (1967): Black, with two stones, wins by 18.

games.title: Three stones (1)
games.note: Black, with three stones, wins by 38 (1967).

games.title: Three stones (2)
games.note: Black, with three stones, wins by 35 (1967).

games.title: Four stones (1)
games.note: Black, with four stones, wins by 42 (1967).

games.title: Four stones (2)
games.note: Black, with four stones, wins by 53 (1967).

games.title: Four stones (3): a close finish
games.note: Black, with four stones, wins by only 2 (1975).

games.title: Five stones (1)
games.note: Black, with five stones, wins by 68 (1967).

games.title: Five stones (2)
games.note: Black, with five stones, wins by 58 (1967).

games.title: Five stones (3)
games.note: Black, with five stones, wins by 57 (1995).

games.title: Six stones
games.note: Black, with six stones, wins by 66 (1967).

games.title: Seven stones
games.note: Black, with seven stones, wins by 92 (1966).

games.title: Nine stones
games.note: Black, with nine stones, wins by 124 (1966).

games.title: A three-stone teaching game (1958)
games.note: Black, with three stones, wins by resignation after 154 moves.

games.title: A three-stone teaching game (1961)
games.note: Koyama Yasuo teaches H. Taylor, who has Black and three stones, and wins by 2.

games.title: A five-stone teaching game (1957)
games.note: White wins by resignation even though Black started with five stones.

games.title: A trial game for the Kitani school (1959)
games.note: Kato Masao, later a top professional, played this game for entry to the Kitani school. Black had four stones and won by 3.
games.event: Trial game for entry to Kitani school

categories.title: Early and ancient games
categories.blurb: Some of the oldest game records that survive, from China and from the first years of the Japanese houses.

games.title: A game dated 1582
games.note: Dated 20 June 1582, one of the oldest dated records in this collection. No result is recorded.

games.title: A castle game of 1706
games.note: Honinbo Dochi (Black) beats Yasui Senkaku by one point in a 281-move castle game.

games.title: A challenge match of 1739
games.note: The first game of a long challenge match between Honinbo Shuhaku and Inoue Shunseki Inseki. Black wins by 10.

games.title: The Rotten Axe-handle Game
games.note: Named after an old Chinese legend of a woodcutter who watched immortals play and found his axe handle had rotted away. Black wins by 1.

games.title: The Four Immortals relay game (1094)
games.note: A relay game with two players on each side. White wins by 1.
games.event: Relay game "The Four Immortals meet in Chengdu"

games.title: Shi Dingan against Fan Xiping (1739)
games.note: The tenth game of a ten-game match between two leading Chinese masters. 341 moves; Black wins by 5.

categories.title: The Edo masters
categories.blurb: The masters of the four Go houses (see the History of Go). Honinbo Dosaku, the young Shusaku and others, and the game behind the "blood-vomiting" legend.

games.title: Dosaku wins a castle game (1668)
games.note: Honinbo Dosaku (Black) beats Yasui Santetsu II by 10 in a castle game.

games.title: Dosaku wins by 13 (1669)
games.note: A 141-move castle game against Yasui Santetsu II.

games.title: Dosaku in 1674
games.note: Dosaku (Black) beats Yasui Santetsu II by 12 in 272 moves.

games.title: Dosaku gives two stones (1696)
games.note: Dosaku, as White, gives Yasui Senkaku two stones, and loses by one point.

games.title: The blood-vomiting game (1835)
games.note: Honinbo Jowa (White) beats Akaboshi Intetsu in 246 moves played over four sessions in August 1835. The game is named after the story that Intetsu coughed blood.

games.title: The game that launched the Hoensha (1879)
games.note: Played to launch the Hoensha, a Go society that lasted until the Nihon Ki-in replaced it in 1924 (see the History of Go). Hayashi Shuei (Black) beats Murase Shuho, the master who taught Oscar Korschelt.

games.title: The ear-reddening game (1846)
games.note: The young Shusaku (Black) beats Inoue Gennan Inseki by 2 points in 325 moves. Named after Shusaku's move 127, said to have made Gennan's ears turn red.

games.title: A castle game against Yasui Sanchi (1849)
games.note: Shusaku (Black) wins by 11. He won all 19 of the castle games in this collection.

games.title: A castle game won by resignation (1849 to 1850)
games.note: Shusaku (Black) beats Sakaguchi Sentoku in 131 moves.

games.title: The longest castle game here (1850)
games.note: 342 moves; Shusaku (Black) beats Ito Showa by 3.

games.title: Shusaku as White (1852)
games.note: Shusaku, playing White, beats Inoue Matsumoto Inseki by 2 in a castle game.

games.title: A 121-move castle game (1853)
games.note: Shusaku (Black) beats Sakaguchi Sentoku by resignation.

games.title: Shusaku wins by one point (1853)
games.note: As White, Shusaku beats Yasui Sanchi by a single point in a castle game.

games.title: A castle game of 1858
games.note: Shusaku, as White, beats Sakaguchi Sentoku by 3.

categories.title: Draws (jigo)
categories.blurb: A jigo is a draw: both sides finish on the same score. Modern games with komi cannot end this way, but older games had none.

games.title: A jigo around 1580
games.note: Hayashi Rigen (Black) and Honinbo Sansa draw after 162 moves.

games.title: A jigo in a ten-game match (1706)
games.note: Honinbo Dochi (Black) draws with Inoue Dosetsu Inseki in 265 moves.

games.title: A jigo in a challenge match (1740)
games.note: Honinbo Shuhaku (Black) and Inoue Shunseki Inseki draw after 287 moves.

games.title: Shusaku draws with Ota Yuzo (1846)
games.note: 260 moves, ending in jigo.

games.title: A drawn game in a ten-game match (1930)
games.note: Nozawa Chikucho and Suzuki Tamejiro draw after 299 moves.

games.title: Kitani and Go Seigen draw (1933)
games.note: Kitani Minoru and Go Seigen draw in 267 moves in the Oteai.

games.title: Maeda Nobuaki and Go Seigen draw (1934)
games.note: A drawn game of 246 moves.

games.title: Fujisawa Kuranosuke and Go Seigen draw (1936)
games.note: A drawn game of 200 moves, recorded as probably an Oteai game.

categories.title: The twentieth century
categories.blurb: From the new ways of opening in the 1930s to unusual board sizes.

games.title: Go Seigen against Kitani, 1933
games.note: The first game of a ten-game match between Go Seigen and Kitani Minoru, the two players who developed the "new fuseki" style. Go Seigen (Black) wins by resignation.

games.title: Go Seigen against Honinbo Shusai (1933)
games.note: A game with Honinbo Shusai played over more than three months, from 16 October 1933 to 29 January 1934. Shusai (White) wins by 2.

games.title: Go Seigen and Kitani together (1934)
games.note: A consultation game: Go Seigen and Kitani Minoru play as a team against Segoe Kensaku and Suzuki Tamejiro, and win by 1.

games.title: A radio game (1935)
games.note: Go Seigen (Black) beats Kitani Minoru by 2 in 305 moves.

games.title: The Showa match (1939)
games.note: A game from the seven-game "Showa Match" between Go Seigen and Kitani Minoru. Go Seigen (Black) wins by resignation.

games.title: The first Honinbo tournament (1939)
games.note: Go Seigen (White) beats Hashimoto Utaro by 4.5.

games.title: Shusai's retirement game (1938)
games.note: Kitani Minoru (Black) beats Honinbo Shusai by 5 in 237 moves, played between July and December 1938. It was Shusai's retirement game, which Kawabata Yasunari turned into the novel "The Master of Go".

games.title: Two future stars as trainees (1965)
games.note: Kobayashi Koichi (White) beats Cho Hunhyun by 4.5 in an insei (trainee) tournament. Both later became world-class professionals.

games.title: A Western player's qualification game (1978)
games.note: Manfred Wimmer (Black, with two stones) plays Tono Hiroaki in a professional qualification game and loses by 3.

games.title: A professional 13×13 game (2014)
games.note: Cho Chikun (Black) plays O Meien in a 13×13 tournament for professionals. White wins by resignation after 114 moves.

games.title: A one-and-a-half point finish on 13×13 (2014)
games.note: Ishida Yoshio (Black) beats Yamashita Keigo by 1.5 in the same 13×13 tournament for professionals, after 106 moves.

categories.title: International finals and modern stars
categories.blurb: Games from the big international tournaments, from the 1980s to today.

games.title: Takemiya wins the first Fujitsu Cup (1988)
games.note: Takemiya Masaki (Black) beats Rin Kaiho by resignation in the final.

games.title: The first Ing Cup, final game 4 (1989)
games.note: A 318-move game: Cho Hunhyun (Black) beats Nie Weiping by 1.

games.title: The first Ing Cup, deciding game (1989)
games.note: Cho Hunhyun (Black) beats Nie Weiping by resignation and wins the final 3 games to 2.

games.title: Cho Chikun and Seo Bongsoo (1992)
games.note: A 313-move semifinal that Cho Chikun (Black) wins by a single point.

games.title: Lee Changho beats Ma Xiaochun (1996)
games.note: Lee Changho (Black) wins the Fujitsu Cup final by resignation.

games.title: Lee Changho against Chang Hao (2000)
games.note: Game 2 of the 4th Ing Cup final: Lee (Black) wins by 1 in 328 moves. Lee went on to win the final 3 games to 1.

games.title: The two Lees (2008)
games.note: Lee Changho (Black) beats Lee Sedol by resignation in a 295-move Ing Cup semifinal.

games.title: Gu Li wins the Fujitsu Cup (2008)
games.note: Gu Li (Black) beats Lee Changho by resignation in the final.

games.title: Lee Sedol wins the Fujitsu Cup (2010)
games.note: Lee Sedol (White) beats Kong Jie by 12.5 in the final.

games.title: Gu Li and Lee Sedol (2012)
games.note: A 291-move game that Gu Li (Black) wins by 5.5.

games.title: The 8th Ing Cup, deciding game (2016)
games.note: Tang Weixing (Black) beats Park Junghwan by 5 in 313 moves and wins the final 3 games to 2.

games.title: A 300-move Samsung Cup final game (2023)
games.note: Ding Hao (Black) beats Xie Erhao by resignation in game 3 of the final, which he won 2 games to 1.

games.title: Ichiriki Ryo against Xie Ke (2024)
games.note: The first game of the 10th Ing Cup final: 341 moves, and Ichiriki (Black) wins by 1. He won the final 3 games to 0.

categories.title: Humans against AlphaGo
categories.blurb: The matches in which a computer program beat professionals (see the History of Go).

games.title: AlphaGo against Fan Hui, game 1 (October 2015)
games.note: The first game of the match in which AlphaGo beat the European champion Fan Hui 5 games to 0. AlphaGo (White) wins by 2.5.

games.title: Lee Sedol against AlphaGo, game 1 (9 March 2016)
games.note: AlphaGo (White) wins by resignation in the first game of the match in Seoul.

games.title: Game 2: "move 37"
games.note: AlphaGo (Black) wins by resignation. According to DeepMind, its move 37 had about a one in 10,000 chance of being played by a human.

games.title: Game 3: AlphaGo wins the match
games.note: AlphaGo (White) wins again, which settles the match 3 games to 0.

games.title: Game 4: Lee Sedol's "God's Touch"
games.note: Lee Sedol (White) wins by resignation. According to DeepMind, his move 78 also had about a one in 10,000 chance of being played.

games.title: Game 5: AlphaGo wins 4 games to 1
games.note: AlphaGo (White) wins the last game, in 280 moves.

categories.title: Rules and curiosities
categories.blurb: Games that went wrong, or right, in unusual ways. Several are void (no result) because play went round in circles.

games.title: The longest game in the collection
games.note: 431 moves in a 2021 Taiwanese women's tournament. Yang Zixuan (Black) beats Zhang Kaixin by 3.5.
games.event: 7th Taiwan Women's Strongest, loser section round 2

games.title: A quintuple ko (2013)
games.note: Five kos at once. The game was declared void.

games.title: Eternal life (1989)
games.note: A shape that can repeat for ever, in a trainee tournament game. The game was declared void.

games.title: A triple ko (2006)
games.note: A game with a triple ko: Cho U (Black) beats Gu Li by 5.5 in 323 moves.

games.title: A triple ko from 1724
games.note: A 92-move record of Nagano Kaizen against Inoue Shunseki, declared void because of a triple ko.

games.title: Both players lose (1930)
games.note: According to the record, both players decided to take a break and sleep, which was against the rules, so both lost.

games.title: The opponent fell asleep (1980)
games.note: Ushinohama Satsuo fell asleep during the dinner break of a Tengen game and could not be found, so Yamabe Toshiro won on time.

games.title: White plays out of turn (1987)
games.note: In a Meijin title game, White (Rin Kaiho) played move 189 when it was not his turn after the dinner break, and lost by forfeit.

games.title: A score with fractions (1988)
games.note: Ing Cup rules (komi 8) can give fractional scores. Cho Hunhyun (Black) beats Kobayashi Koichi by 1 5/6.

games.title: A win that is not a loss for Black (1928)
games.note: A two-stone game with an unusual result: White wins, but "Black does not lose".
